correctness.rationale: For nonscalar x in M_2(F_q), the centralizer is span{I,x} and has dimension two. Trace cyclicity shows im(ad_x) is contained in the trace-orthogonal complement of the centralizer; equal dimensions give equality. For traceless r this reduces fiber existence to tr(rx)=0. A nonzero trace functional has a q^3-element kernel containing exactly q scalar matrices, so exactly q^3-q vertices have a nonempty r-fiber. Every such fiber is a q^2-element affine centralizer coset. Substitution into the published general degree formula gives the stated characteristic-two and odd-characteristic values. The r=0 and nontraceless cases follow from centralizer sizes and trace-zero of commutators. The packaged exhaustive checks match every formula over F2, F3, F4, and F5.

value.rationale: The primary paper introduces a graph whose degree formula is only as explicit as the generalized-centralizer fibers. For the fundamental simple algebra M_2(F_q), the theorem solves those fibers completely for every parameter r and every finite field, yielding an exact degree multiset with a sharp characteristic-two boundary. It also exposes a reusable linear-algebraic mechanism: one trace hyperplane controls all exceptional vertices, uniformly across nilpotent, semisimple, and in characteristic two even scalar nonzero commutators.
